dohGuide.title: How to Enable DNS over HTTPS (DoH) in Chrome
dohGuide.intro: Follow these steps to enable secure DNS (DoH) in your Chrome browser:
dohGuide.step2: 2. Search for 'security' in the settings search bar.
dohGuide.step3: 3. Scroll down to the 'Advanced' section and find 'Use secure DNS'.
dohGuide.step4: 4. Enable 'Use secure DNS' and select 'With custom provider'.
dohGuide.step5: 5. Enter the HTTPS address provided by your preferred DoH provider.
dohGuide.done: Follow the steps in Chrome settings to enable DNS over HTTPS.

common.simulated_dns_warning: Note: Chrome extensions cannot change DNS directly. Please set DNS manually or use DoH.

dohPoll.q1: Did you know Chrome can use DNS over HTTPS?
dohPoll.q2: Would you like to see a step-by-step DoH activation guide?
dohPoll.notifyBody: DNS over HTTPS encrypts requests between Chrome and the resolver, but the provider can still see them.
steps: Go to Chrome Security Settings.
In the Advanced section, find Use secure DNS.
In Custom provider, enter the HTTPS address provided by your preferred DNS-over-HTTPS provider.
dohPoll.note: Apply any DNS changes manually in Chrome settings. This extension does not change DNS settings.
